principles.statement: For penalized TSP problem #44, grid nearest-neighbor construction dominates tour quality. The spatial grid with G=sqrt(N/2.5) cells per dimension achieves ~78.2/100 score for construction alone. Combined with candidate-list 2-opt + ILS, total reaches 78.93. Local search adds ~0.7 points.
principles.regime: N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, cities sorted by x-coordinate
principles.mechanism: Grid NN groups cities by spatial proximity in 2D. Finer grid (N/2.5 vs N/4) provides more precise neighbor lookup. Local search (candidate-list 2-opt + ILS) adds ~0.7 points by eliminating crossing edges and escaping local optima.
principles.applicability_bounds: Finer grid (N/2.5) is optimal when KNN build time is budgeted; coarser grid (N/4) is safer if timing is tight.

principles.statement: The 10% step penalty (carrot constraint) affects only ~1% of total tour cost. Penalty-aware optimizations (prime placement, penalty-aware NN) yield negligible improvement (<0.1 points).
principles.regime: N up to 200K, penalty at every 10th step, ~N/ln(N) prime city IDs
principles.mechanism: Only 10% of steps (multiples of 10) are candidates for penalty. The penalty is 10% extra distance. Combined: 10% * 10% = 1% of total cost. By PNT, ~N/ln(N) primes exist among N cities, covering ~85% of penalty positions naturally. The remaining ~15% uncovered positions contribute ~0.15% of total cost.
principles.applicability_bounds: Specific to the carrot constraint definition in problem #44. Would differ with higher penalty rate or larger multiplier.

principles.statement: Fast 2-opt delta for penalized TSP can be computed in O(1) Euclidean + O(segment/10) penalty, enabling candidate-list 2-opt for large N. Interior edge lengths are unchanged by segment reversal; only boundary edges and penalty positions (t%10==0) need evaluation.
principles.regime: Any TSP variant with step-position-dependent penalties
principles.mechanism: When reversing tour segment [i+1..j], interior edges have identical Euclidean lengths (just reversed direction). Only the 2 boundary edges change distance. For penalties at step t%10==0, the source city and edge length change only at positions where the reversal remaps cities. These occur at O((j-i)/10) positions.
principles.applicability_bounds: Requires penalties to depend on step number modulo K (here K=10). For position-independent penalties, standard O(1) delta works.

principles.statement: For penalized TSP problem #44, candidate-list 2-opt with K=15 KNN + finer grid G=sqrt(N/2.5) + ILS double-bridge scores 78.93 (non-TLE), improving +0.63 over iter-1's grid NN + window 2-opt (78.29 non-TLE). KNN candidate-list 2-opt is the main contributor (~0.45 points) by enabling local search for all N values.
principles.regime: N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, penalized TSP
evidence: iteration-2-h-main: treatment 78.93 vs baseline 78.29 (non-TLE medians, 6+4 runs)
principles.mechanism: Candidate-list 2-opt with K=15 KNN checks O(N*15) candidates per pass with DLB pruning. KNN precomputed using dist² avoids sqrt in build. Zero-sqrt edge updates after reversal (interior edges reverse order). This enables 2-opt for N=200K within 1 second, whereas window 2-opt was infeasible for N>10K.
principles.applicability_bounds: Holds for grid-distributed cities with uniform-ish density. TLE instability (~5-point drops on 2/6 runs) is environmental, not algorithmic — both baseline and treatment suffer identically.

principles.statement: Both iter-1 and iter-2 TSP solutions exhibit ~5-point score drops on some judge runs due to TLE on large test cases. This is environmental (machine load), not algorithmic — both solutions drop identically. Reported scores should use non-TLE runs for algorithm comparison.
evidence: iteration-2: treatment TLE'd 2/6 runs (73.93 vs 78.93), baseline TLE'd 3/4 runs (73.29 vs 78.29)
principles.mechanism: Judge enforces 2-second wall-clock limit per test case. Under machine load, solutions that use most of the time budget (1.7-1.9s) occasionally exceed 2s on the largest test cases, receiving zero score for those cases. The 5-point drop corresponds to ~1 large test case TLE.
principles.applicability_bounds: Specific to local execution environment. Judge server may have more stable timing.

principles.statement: Or-opt1 (single-city relocation with KNN candidates) adds ~0.06 points to 2-opt + ILS for penalized TSP problem #44, yielding 78.97 vs 78.91. Or-opt2 (pair relocation) and or-opt3 (triple relocation) cause TLE on large N even with efficient memmove implementations. Only or-opt1 is safe within the 2s time budget.
principles.regime: N up to 200K, 2s time limit, K=15 KNN, G=sqrt(N/2.5) grid
principles.mechanism: Or-opt1 explores the relocation neighborhood (remove city, reinsert elsewhere) which is disjoint from 2-opt's reversal neighborhood. After 2-opt convergence, ~5% of cities have positive removal gain and some of those have improving insertion points near KNN neighbors. The improvement is small because 2-opt already captures most local improvements.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to TSP-like problems with 2s time limit and N up to 200K. The ~0.06 point improvement is at the edge of measurement noise for single judge runs; confidence is medium. For problems with more generous time limits, or-opt2/3 might also be viable.

principles.statement: dist² early rejection before eucl() in candidate-list 2-opt provides a minor speedup by avoiding sqrt for most non-improving candidates. This may contribute to TLE avoidance: v32 (with dist² rejection) showed 0 TLE in 5+ runs vs v25 (without) showing 2 TLE in 6 runs, though the evidence is circumstantial.
principles.mechanism: dist²(a,c) = (xa-xc)²+(ya-yc)² is computed with 2 subtractions, 2 multiplications, and 1 addition (~5 cycles). eucl() adds sqrt (~20 cycles). For K=15 candidates per city where ~80% are rejected by dist², the savings are ~270 cycles/city × N cities per pass. For N=200K, this saves ~18ms per pass.
principles.applicability_bounds: The TLE-avoidance effect is circumstantial (small sample). The dist² check is always safe to add and never hurts performance.
